bib.title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning", Alexis Fox, Junlin Wang, Paul Rosu, Bhuwan Dhingra (all Duke University). Preprint, arXiv 2607.20064v3 [cs.AI], 12 Oct 2026.
COVERAGE: 23 of 23 pages, all 65,447 chars read (body, references, Appendices A-C incl. prompts). Figures are extracted as text only; I did not render them.

MAIN CLAIM: An agent that appends every observation, action and outcome to a lossless log (write) and searches it with code such as grep and Python (read) beats the same coding agent without a log. It matches specialized ARC-AGI-3 harnesses at far lower token cost. It is a "fidelity-tractability" argument: don't summarize at write time, make read programmatic.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
1. ARC-AGI-3, 25 public games, 500-action cap, high reasoning effort. PRO-LONG beats the no-log coding agent by 15.7-21.0 pp at pass@1 across GPT-5.5 (Codex), Opus 4.6 and Fable 5 (abstract: "18.0 percentage points" on average). GPT-5.5: 41.2 vs 24.0 (n=5 PRO-LONG, CIs reported).
2. Cost: against WorldModeler (GPT-5.5) it scores 41.2 vs 45.1 pass@1 with 5.8x fewer billed tokens. Against Schema (Claude Code) it scores 82.1 vs 84.4 best@2 with 4.2x fewer. Opus 4.6: 42.4 vs Arcgentica 39.0 pass@1. Competitor runs were rescored by the authors. Fable 5 at 2,000 actions: 97.4% best@2 for about $1,750 (a lower bound, since several games were not rerun). Schema's 99.0 cost $6,447.
3. NetHack (BALROG progression, 5-episode "lifetimes" on a fixed seed, log kept across episodes). GPT-5.6+Codex (n=10 lifetimes): mean best@5 is 24.5% vs 13.5% no-log. Kimi+Mini-SWE (n=15): 11.3% vs 5.1%. Best single episode 25.7% vs prior published best 20.6%; best lifetime 40.8%.
4. Ablations (GPT-5.5):
- Tool ladder: read only 23.1, +grep 27.2, +Python 38.3, +write/edit 41.2.
- Dropping the accessed context (compaction threshold) from 244K to 64K: PRO-LONG scores 44.3 vs 41.2 (within its CI), while no-log falls monotonically.
- With Kimi, 1M to 100K: PRO-LONG moves by 0.3 points, no-log drops more than 5.
- Clearing the workspace every call: PRO-LONG 40.7 vs 41.2, no-log 19.9 vs 24.0.
- Best@5 is 60.1 vs 41.2 pass@1, so run-to-run variance is large.

QUOTES
- p.2: "This creates a fidelity–tractability tradeoff. Reducing what is saved at write time makes read easier, but can discard details whose relevance is evident only in hindsight."
- p.8: "PRO-LONG does not degrade, scoring slightly higher at 64K than at the default (44.3% vs. 41.2%, within its confidence interval), while no-log falls monotonically."

LIMITS / NOT SHOWN
- Only two game benchmarks (ARC-AGI-3, NetHack). Nothing on conversational, personal or user-preference memory, or on semantic or vector retrieval baselines head to head. MemGPT, Mem0 etc. are discussed but not run; the baselines are no-log and other game harnesses.
- The no-log baseline can still write notes; the paper's own baseline is a stronger coding agent, not a memory system.
- Small samples: n=5 or fewer on ARC, 2 runs on Claude Code, n=1 on several context-ablation points. Large variance; pass@1 and best@k gaps are wide.
- Cost comparisons depend on the authors' rescoring and billed-token weighting. Prior harnesses lack replicates and have unstated selection procedures. Schema's cost covers only retained runs.
- Models released after the benchmark may advantage all agents (conceded).
- It requires a coding agent with a shell and Python; logs reached 320K lines. Per-game logs are not shared across games. Authors list RL and co-training as future work.
- Each game's log is a single-task trajectory, so "memory" here is within-task history, not cross-task knowledge. The NetHack cross-episode test reuses a fixed seed.

BUILDS ON
MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023), Generative Agents (Park et al., UIST 2023), Mem0 (Chhikara et al., ECAI 2025), ReasoningBank (Ouyang et al., ICLR 2026), SkillRL (Xia et al. 2026), RAG (Lewis et al., NeurIPS 2020), memory survey (Zhang et al. 2025b, ACM TOIS), context-engineering survey (Mei et al. 2025). Programmatic line: Recursive Language Models (Zhang, Kraska, Khattab 2025), "Coding agents are effective long-context processors" (Cao et al. 2026). Context rot: Hong et al. 2025 (Chroma); lost in the middle: Liu et al., TACL 2024. Benchmarks: ARC-AGI-3 (ARC Prize Foundation 2026), NetHack Learning Environment (Küttler et al., NeurIPS 2020), BALROG (Paglieri et al., ICLR 2025). Baselines: WorldModeler (Rodionov 2026), Arcgentica (Symbolica 2026), Schema (Zeng et al. 2026), Glyphbox (Vaguely Aligned 2026).

FIGURE CANDIDATES
- Fig. 1 (p.2): the architecture. Accessed context (~100K-1M tokens) vs accessible context (10M+), with log.txt and the read/grep/bash tool space. This is the best match for the note's accessed/accessible framing.
- Fig. 5 (p.7): pass@1 vs accessed-context size; PRO-LONG stays flat while no-log degrades.
- Table 2 (p.9): the tool-ladder numbers.

PROBLEMS: None with extraction. The model names (Fable 5, GPT-5.6, Opus 4.8, Kimi K3) are as printed and are not mine to verify. No embedded instructions found. The prompts in Appendix C are the paper's own agent prompts, not directed at me.
